correctness.rationale: If x is Birkhoff-orthogonal to y and orthogonality is symmetric, then the second skew norm ||beta x-alpha y|| is simultaneously at least beta and at least alpha. The first skew norm is at most alpha+beta, which gives the sharp structural upper bound min{1,beta/alpha}. For the affine-regular hexagon, a complete support-functional classification proves symmetric Birkhoff orthogonality. The pair x=(1,0), y=(0,-1) is Birkhoff-orthogonal and has skew norms alpha+beta and max{alpha,beta}, so it attains the bound for every positive alpha,beta.
risks: The term Radon plane is used only for the two-dimensional symmetric-Birkhoff setting; the structural inequality itself is stated in the more general symmetry form.
The checker verifies the finite facet/support geometry, while the all-parameter inequality is proved symbolically in RESULT.md rather than by sampling.

value.rationale: The defining paper introduces B_{alpha-beta} specifically to quantify the mismatch between Birkhoff and skew orthogonality. The new theorem shows that symmetry of Birkhoff orthogonality itself imposes a parameter-sensitive sharp envelope, improving the published universal bound on an entire half of parameter space. The affine-regular hexagon is the canonical non-Hilbert Radon polytope and attains that envelope for every parameter pair, giving a complete benchmark profile rather than a single value. The result cleanly separates the effect of orthogonality symmetry from Hilbertianity.
risks: The structural improvement is elementary once Birkhoff symmetry is recognized, so its value lies in the sharp parameter envelope and canonical exact profile rather than technical depth.
